questions.q: In surface anatomy, the spleen lies along the axis of which ribs?
questions.exp: Surface anatomy: location — along axis of 9th-11th ribs. (Book p260)

questions.q: Which border of the spleen has a notch?
questions.exp: Surface anatomy: border — the inferolateral border has a notch. (Book p260)

questions.q: Splenomegaly displaces the spleen in which direction?
questions.exp: Applied aspect: splenic enlargement is medially. (Book p260)

questions.q: Downward displacement of the spleen is prevented by which ligament?
questions.exp: Applied aspect: downward displacement is prevented by the phrenicocolic ligament. (Book p260)

questions.q: Splenic trauma is classically associated with fractures of which ribs?
opts: 9th to 11th ribs on the left side
9th to 11th ribs on the right side
questions.exp: Applied aspect: fracture of 9th-11th ribs on the left side leads to splenic trauma. (Book p260)

questions.q: Which of the splenic ligaments are avascular and can be cut directly?
questions.exp: Splenic ligaments table: splenophrenic and splenocolic — avascular, the ligament can be cut. (Book p260)

questions.q: The gastrosplenic ligament contains which vessels?
questions.exp: Splenic ligaments table: gastrosplenic ligament carries the short gastric vessels. (Book p260)

questions.q: The lienorenal ligament transmits all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Splenic ligaments table: lienorenal ligament carries the splenic vessels and the tail of the pancreas — the gastroduodenal vessels are not in it. (Book p260)

questions.q: Before the lienorenal ligament is cut, what must be done to its contents?
opts: Vessels are ligated and then the ligament is cut
The ligament is cut first and the vessels tied later
Only the tail of the pancreas is divided
No ligation is needed as it is avascular
questions.exp: Splenic ligaments table: gastrosplenic and lienorenal contents (short gastric vessels, splenic vessels, tail of pancreas) — vessels are ligated and then the ligament is cut. (Book p260)

questions.q: The splenic artery is a branch of:
questions.exp: Blood supply of spleen: splenic artery — a branch of the coeliac trunk. (Book p260)

questions.q: The portal vein is formed by the union of the splenic vein with which vein?
questions.exp: Blood supply: splenic vein — the portal vein is formed by the splenic vein joining the superior mesenteric vein. (Book p260)

questions.q: The inferior mesenteric vein drains into:
questions.exp: Blood supply: inferior mesenteric vein drains into the splenic vein. (Book p260)

questions.q: The immunological function of the spleen is to:
questions.exp: Functions: 1. Immunological — produces antibodies. (Book p261)

questions.q: After splenectomy, the risk of which type of infection rises?

questions.q: The spleen acts as a 'graveyard' for blood cells by:
questions.exp: Functions: 2. Acts as graveyard for blood cells — filters the non-functioning cells. (Book p261)

questions.q: Physiological haematopoiesis by the spleen occurs in:

The 3rd to 5th month of fetal life

questions.q: Pathological haematopoiesis by the spleen is seen in:
questions.exp: Functions: pathological haematopoiesis occurs in myeloproliferative diseases. (Book p261)

questions.q: The reservoir function of the spleen is for:
questions.exp: Functions: 4. Reservoir function for WBCs, RBCs and platelets. (Book p261)

A permanent fall in all cell lines

questions.q: Splenunculi are:

A true cyst lined by mesothelium
A cyst of flattened squamous epithelium

questions.q: A splenic artery aneurysm is the most common:

Occur in children with frequent rupture

Is always asymptomatic and never treated

units.title: Anatomy of the Spleen
units.guide: The spleen hides behind the 9th to 11th ribs, so fractures of those left ribs are splenic injuries, and its inferolateral border carries the notch. The gastrosplenic and lienorenal ligaments hold vessels and the pancreatic tail, so they are ligated before being cut, while the splenophrenic and splenocolic ligaments are avascular and can be divided freely. The splenic artery rides out of the coeliac trunk, and the portal vein is born where the splenic vein meets the superior mesenteric vein — the IMV joining the splenic vein on the way.

units.title: Functions of the Spleen
units.guide: The spleen makes antibodies, acts as the graveyard that filters spent blood cells, haematopoieses in the 3rd-5th week of fetal life (and pathologically in myeloproliferative disease), and banks WBCs, RBCs and platelets. Take it away and opportunistic infections loom while blood counts rise transiently.

units.title: Applied Aspects of Splenic Tissue
units.sec: Applied Aspects of Splenic Tissue · p261
units.guide: Left-behind accessory splenic tissue — splenunculi, most often at the hilum — can make an ITP come back, so the spleen bed is searched carefully. Splenosis is different: trauma seeds the omentum and bowel with splenic tissue that mimics a tumour on imaging but is normal splenic tissue on biopsy.

units.title: Splenic Cysts
units.guide: Pseudocysts are post-traumatic false cysts, unlined by epithelium, that smooth out on CT and resolve on their own. True cysts — hydatid, dermoid and epidermoid — behave differently: a hydatid with multiple daughter cysts needs splenectomy under albendazole cover, and a squamous-lined epidermoid cyst over 5 cm that is symptomatic is excised.

units.title: Splenic Artery Aneurysm
units.guide: The splenic artery is the commonest site of visceral artery aneurysm, born of pancreatitis, trauma, atherosclerosis or pregnancy — and in pregnancy it ruptures in the 2nd-3rd trimester. Most stay silent; rupture brings pain and Kehr's sign. CT angiography diagnoses it, embolisation or grafting is first line, and splenectomy is the last resort.

units.title: Splenic Infarct
units.guide: Splenic infarcts follow hypersplenism of portal hypertension or myelodysplastic syndromes and mostly stay silent. When they speak, it is with LUQ pain, pleuritic pain and shoulder-tip referral. CECT shows the hypodense infarcted spleen; treat conservatively and operate only if symptoms persist or an abscess supervenes.

units.title: Splenic Abscess
units.guide: The splenic abscess is the infection of the immunocompromised and the post-infarct spleen — high-grade fever, pleuritic pain, and a CECT hypodense collection of necrotic debris. A pigtail catheter drains it before anyone thinks of removing the spleen.

units.title: Splenectomy: Indications
units.guide: Trauma is the commonest reason the spleen comes out, followed by oncology — en bloc with gastric and pancreatic cancers — and haematology: spherocytosis, ITP and hypersplenism, plus left-sided portal hypertension from splenic vein thrombosis. Among splenic tumours, haemangioma is the commonest benign lesion and needs nothing, while lymphoma, the commonest malignancy, answers to chemotherapy and is rarely operated on.

units.title: Splenectomy: Steps and Complications
units.guide: Splenectomy runs in five steps: dissection of the aspect of spleen, lateral and retroperitoneal attachments, transection of the hilum, the short gastric vessels, and removal. Its complications are a teaching list — pancreatic tail injury with amylase-rich drain, gastric haematemesis when short gastric vessels are ligated, a transient trilineage count rise mistaken for infection, platelets over 10 lakh predisposing to thrombosis (aspirin), permanent Howell Jolly bodies on smear, and the commonest of all: left lower lobe atelectasis, prevented by incentive spirometry and pain control.

units.title: OPSI: Post-Splenectomy Sepsis and Vaccination
units.sec: OPSI: Post-Splenectomy Sepsis and Vaccination · p264
units.guide: OPSI — opportunistic overwhelming post splenectomy infection — is the lethal shadow of the operation: encapsulated bacteria (pneumococcus above all, then meningococcus and H. influenzae), striking children more than adults, mostly within the first 2 years, with higher mortality after haematological indications. Vaccinate: pneumococcal and meningococcal repeated every 5 years, H. influenzae every 10 years, influenza yearly — 2 weeks before if elective, post op day 1/2 if emergency.
